## Q ai-20261022-a31-01
- domain: performance
- task: 3.1
- topic: storage
- services: EBS, EC2
- tags: ebs-volume-types, elastic-volumes
- difficulty: hard
- skills: 3.1.s1, 3.1.k2
- concept: gp3 (up to 80,000 IOPS and 2,000 MiB/s, independent of size) changed online with Elastic Volumes beats resizing gp2 or paying for io2 Block Express when the numbers fit gp3
- refs: 02-storage-services.md, R-performance-benchmarks.md
- hint: So IOPS và throughput cần có với giới hạn hiện hành của gp2, gp3, io2 — loại nào đủ, rẻ nhất và đổi được khi DB vẫn chạy?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 140

A logistics company runs a self-managed PostgreSQL database on a large Nitro-based Amazon EC2 instance. The 3 TiB data volume is a General Purpose SSD (gp2) volume, and month-end batch jobs now saturate it at about 9,000 IOPS and 250 MiB/s. Monitoring shows that the database needs a sustained 45,000 IOPS and 1,200 MiB/s. Single-digit millisecond latency is acceptable, the database cannot be stopped, and the company wants the lowest-cost fix. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

- A. Use Elastic Volumes to change the volume type to io2 Block Express and provision 45,000 IOPS while the instance stays in service.
- B. Use Elastic Volumes to increase the size of the gp2 volume until its baseline performance reaches 45,000 IOPS and 1,200 MiB/s.
- C. Use Elastic Volumes to change the volume type to gp3 and provision 45,000 IOPS and 1,200 MiB/s of throughput on the running volume.
- D. Create four gp2 volumes in a RAID 0 array, copy the database files to the array, and cut the database over during a planned maintenance window.

**Answer:** C

**Explanation:** gp3 can be provisioned up to 80,000 IOPS and 2,000 MiB/s regardless of size, and Elastic Volumes applies the change without stopping the instance, so gp3 meets the numbers at the lowest price.
- io2 Block Express: also works, but nothing requires sub-millisecond latency or more than 80,000 IOPS (tốn chi phí hơn)
- Larger gp2 volume: gp2 tops out at 16,000 IOPS and 250 MiB/s whatever its size (cấu hình không tồn tại)
- RAID 0 of gp2 volumes: needs a data copy and a cutover that stops the database (vi phạm ràng buộc)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-volume-types.html
> 🇻🇳 gp3 chỉnh IOPS/throughput độc lập dung lượng, đổi loại online bằng Elastic Volumes và rẻ hơn io2.

## Q ai-20261022-a31-06
- domain: performance
- task: 3.1
- topic: storage
- services: S3
- tags: s3-prefixes, request-rate
- difficulty: medium
- skills: 3.1.s2, 3.1.s1
- concept: S3 request rates scale per key prefix; 503 Slow Down on one hot prefix is fixed by spreading keys across many prefixes and parallelizing, not by quotas, acceleration or multipart
- refs: 02-storage-services.md, R-performance-benchmarks.md
- hint: Lỗi 503 Slow Down khi mọi khoá bắt đầu giống nhau — S3 mở rộng tốc độ request theo đơn vị nào?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 120

An IoT analytics company ingests sensor files into one Amazon S3 bucket. Thousands of devices upload small objects, and every object key begins with the same date segment, such as 2026-10-22/device-id/file. At peak, the ingestion service sends about 12,000 PUT requests per second to keys that begin with the same date and receives HTTP 503 Slow Down responses. The data must stay in one bucket in the S3 Standard storage class for later queries. Which change will increase the sustained write rate?

- A. Add a short hash to the beginning of each object name so that requests spread across many prefixes, and send the uploads in parallel.
- B. Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket and have the ingestion service send every upload through the bucket's accelerate endpoint.
- C. Switch the ingestion service to multipart upload for every object so that each small file is sent to the bucket in several parts.
- D. Request a service quota increase for the number of PUT requests per second that the bucket is allowed to receive.

**Answer:** A

**Explanation:** S3 scales request rates per key prefix and allows unlimited prefixes, so spreading objects across many prefixes and sending requests in parallel raises the sustained PUT rate.
- Transfer Acceleration: speeds up long-distance transfers, not the request rate against one prefix (giải bài toán khác)
- Multipart upload: meant for large objects and only adds requests for small files (dùng sai tính năng)
- Quota increase: request rates scale per prefix, not through a quota that support can raise (cấu hình không tồn tại)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/optimizing-performance.html
> 🇻🇳 503 Slow Down trên một prefix → rải object ra nhiều prefix và gửi song song; không có quota để nâng tốc độ request.

## Q ai-20261022-a32-04
- domain: performance
- task: 3.2
- topic: compute
- services: Lambda, API Gateway
- tags: lambda-concurrency, snapstart, cold-start
- difficulty: medium
- skills: 3.2.k5, 3.2.s4
- family: lambda-java-cold-start
- concept: For a Java Lambda function, SnapStart removes most of the cold-start delay at no additional charge, which beats provisioned concurrency on cost
- refs: 01-compute-services.md, R-performance-benchmarks.md
- hint: Runtime là Java và đề hỏi phương án tiết kiệm nhất — tính năng nào giảm khởi tạo mà không tính thêm phí cho Java?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 115

A fintech company hosts a customer-facing REST API on AWS Lambda behind Amazon API Gateway. The functions use the Java 17 runtime and load a large dependency framework during start-up, so the first request that reaches each new execution environment takes several seconds. Traffic is spiky: it can jump from a handful of requests to thousands per second within a minute after a push notification. The company wants to remove this start-up delay without rewriting the functions. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

- A. Raise the memory setting of each function to the maximum value so that the start-up code finishes faster on every new execution environment.
- B. Enable Lambda SnapStart on each function, publish a version, and send traffic to that version through an alias.
- C. Set reserved concurrency on each function to the expected peak so that Lambda keeps initialized execution environments ready for traffic.
- D. Configure provisioned concurrency on a published version and adjust it with Application Auto Scaling to match the expected traffic.

**Answer:** B

**Explanation:** For Java runtimes SnapStart adds no extra charge and resumes new execution environments from a cached snapshot of the initialized function, which removes most of the start-up delay.
- Maximum memory: more CPU shortens initialization a little but does not remove it, and every millisecond costs more (dùng sai tính năng)
- Reserved concurrency: only guarantees and caps how many environments can run; it pre-initializes none (dùng sai tính năng)
- Provisioned concurrency: keeps initialized environments ready, but you pay for them all the time (tốn chi phí hơn)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/snapstart.html
> 🇻🇳 Java + cold start + tiết kiệm nhất → SnapStart (không phụ phí cho Java); provisioned concurrency tính tiền liên tục.

## Q ai-20261022-a33-08
- domain: performance
- task: 3.3
- topic: database
- services: DAX, DynamoDB, ElastiCache, Aurora
- tags: caching-strategies, redis-vs-memcached
- difficulty: medium
- skills: 3.3.s5, 3.3.k2
- family: dynamodb-aurora-cache-choice
- concept: ElastiCache is a general-purpose cache usable with any data store, so one layer can serve both DynamoDB and Aurora; DAX caches DynamoDB only
- refs: 03-database-services.md, F-so-sanh-database-theo-dac-diem.md
- hint: Đổi câu hỏi: một lớp cache chung cho cả DynamoDB lẫn Aurora — loại cache nào không bị ràng buộc vào một kho dữ liệu?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 120

A gaming company stores player profiles in an Amazon DynamoDB table and match catalogs in an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. A small set of popular streamer profiles accounts for most profile reads, and the same hot match-catalog queries repeat constantly, so both data stores are slowed by repeated reads. The profile reads are eventually consistent, and the application is written with the AWS SDK for DynamoDB and a MySQL driver. Which solution will accelerate both the profile reads and the catalog queries by using a single caching layer?

- A. Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey cache, check it first on every read, and load it on a miss for both data stores.
- B. Add a second Region with DynamoDB global tables and Aurora Replicas so that reads are served from the Region nearest to each player.
- C. Create an Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster in the VPC and point the application's DynamoDB calls at the DAX endpoint.
- D. Switch the DynamoDB table to provisioned capacity with a high read capacity setting and add a larger Aurora writer instance.

**Answer:** A

**Explanation:** ElastiCache for Valkey is a general-purpose in-memory cache that the application can use with any data store, so one lazy-loading layer can serve both the DynamoDB profiles and the Aurora catalog queries.
- DAX: caches DynamoDB only, so the Aurora queries stay uncached (dùng sai tính năng)
- Second Region with global tables and replicas: moves data closer to players but does not cache repeated reads (giải bài toán khác)
- Higher provisioned capacity and a larger writer: adds throughput, not in-memory read latency (giải bài toán khác)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/WhatIs.html
> 🇻🇳 Một lớp cache dùng chung cho cả DynamoDB và Aurora → ElastiCache (DAX chỉ dành cho DynamoDB).

## Q ai-20261022-a35-05
- domain: performance
- task: 3.5
- topic: analytics
- services: Kinesis Data Streams
- tags: sharding, kinesis-shards, streaming-ingestion
- difficulty: hard
- skills: 3.5.k6, 3.5.s2, 3.5.s6
- concept: A hot partition key can exceed one shard's limit; neither on-demand mode nor more shards fix it, so a higher-cardinality key that keeps per-entity order is needed
- refs: 09-analytics-bigdata.md
- hint: Một khoá phân vùng duy nhất vượt giới hạn của một shard — cần khoá có nhiều giá trị hơn mà vẫn giữ thứ tự theo từng xe.
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 130

A logistics company streams GPS events from 60,000 trucks into a provisioned-mode Kinesis data stream. Producers use the truck's depot ID as the partition key, and about 25 depots exist. One central depot generates more traffic than a single shard can ingest, so producers receive WriteProvisionedThroughputExceeded errors while most other shards are nearly idle. Events from the same truck must be processed in order. Which solution will stop the throttling?

- A. Switch the stream to on-demand capacity mode so that Kinesis Data Streams splits the busy shards automatically as traffic grows
- B. Change the partition key to the truck ID so that records spread across the shards while the events of each truck stay in one shard
- C. Double the shard count by calling UpdateShardCount so that the hash key range of the busy depot's truck events is divided across more shards
- D. Use a random UUID as the partition key for each record of the truck events so that the writes spread evenly across the shards of the stream

**Answer:** B

**Explanation:** A partition key maps to exactly one shard, so a depot whose traffic exceeds one shard cannot be fixed by capacity changes. Truck ID has high cardinality and keeps each truck's events in one shard, preserving order.
- On-demand mode: it cannot split a single hot partition key below one shard's limit (dùng sai tính năng)
- More shards: the busy depot's key still hashes to one shard (dùng sai tính năng)
- Random UUID key: spreads writes but breaks per-truck ordering (vi phạm ràng buộc)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/how-do-i-size-a-stream.html
> 🇻🇳 Hot key vượt giới hạn 1 shard → đổi partition key sang giá trị phân tán hơn nhưng vẫn theo từng xe (giữ thứ tự).

A university is migrating 80 TB of departmental file shares and student home directories to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. Users access the shares over SMB from domain-joined computers, I/O demand is low, and many files are duplicated across departments. The file system must be Multi-AZ so that it survives an Availability Zone failure. The university wants the lowest storage cost. Which TWO configuration choices should a solutions architect make? (Choose TWO)

- A. Enable Data Deduplication on the file system so that duplicated data is stored once.
- B. Deploy the file system as Single-AZ to avoid paying for the standby file server at a low price.
- C. Choose SSD storage with provisioned SSD IOPS so that home directories and departmental shares stay fast.
- D. Provision the maximum throughput capacity so that background jobs that scan duplicated files finish quickly.
- E. Choose the HDD storage type, which suits home directories and departmental shares with low I/O.

**Answer:** A, E

**Explanation:** HDD storage costs less than SSD and fits low-I/O shares, and Data Deduplication stores duplicate content once, cutting the capacity that must be paid for.

- SSD with provisioned IOPS: pays for performance the workload does not use (tốn chi phí hơn)

A retail group has seven business units, each with its own standalone AWS account that is paid with a separate corporate credit card. Together the accounts store about 280 TB in Amazon S3 Standard, but no single account is large enough to reach the lower per-GB price tiers, so every account pays the highest storage rate. The group does not want to move data or change any architecture. Which action will reduce the S3 storage cost?

- A. Move the data of the seven accounts into one account's buckets and grant the other accounts access through bucket policies.
- B. Purchase S3 reserved capacity in each account for a one-year term to receive a discount on the storage that it uses.
- C. Activate cost allocation tags in every account so that the tagged storage qualifies for lower tiered pricing rates.
- D. Create an AWS Organizations organization, invite the seven accounts, and use consolidated billing so that usage is combined.

**Answer:** D

**Explanation:** Consolidated billing combines usage across member accounts, so the group reaches the lower volume price tiers (and shares Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discounts) at no extra fee, with no data movement.

- S3 reserved capacity: S3 has no reserved capacity purchase (cấu hình không tồn tại)
- Cost allocation tags: tags only organize reporting and do not change prices (dùng sai tính năng)

A logistics company's tracking service writes each GPS event, about 2 KB of JSON, to Amazon S3 as its own object. The service produces roughly 150 million events per day, and S3 request charges are now the largest part of the storage bill. Analysts query the data once a day with Amazon Athena, and a delay of a few minutes before events become queryable is acceptable. Which change will reduce the S3 cost the MOST?

- A. Send the events to Amazon Data Firehose, which buffers them and delivers larger compressed objects to the bucket.
- B. Compress the events with gzip before uploading them, and keep writing one object per event to the bucket.
- C. Upload each event with the S3 multipart upload API so that the request is committed as several smaller parts in parallel.
- D. Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket so that each small upload reaches S3 over the AWS edge network.

- Multipart upload per event: adds extra requests for tiny objects (dùng sai tính năng)
- Transfer Acceleration: adds a per-GB fee and does not reduce requests (giải bài toán khác)

- refs: 02-storage-services.md

A document-management company stores customer files in an Amazon S3 bucket that has versioning enabled. The application overwrites files often, so older versions pile up and storage costs keep rising. Staff open current files throughout the day, and users upload large videos with multipart uploads that are frequently abandoned halfway. The company needs only the previous 30 days of versions for undo and wants to cut storage cost without changing the application. Which TWO S3 Lifecycle actions should a solutions architect configure? (Choose TWO)

- A. Transition current object versions to S3 Glacier Deep Archive a few days after they are created.
- B. Expire noncurrent object versions 30 days after they become noncurrent.
- C. Disable versioning on the bucket so that overwrites stop creating new versions.
- D. Abort incomplete uploads that remain unfinished beyond a set number of days.
- E. Transition every object version to S3 One Zone-IA immediately after upload.

**Answer:** B, D

**Explanation:** Expiring noncurrent versions after the undo window removes storage nobody needs, and the abort-incomplete-multipart-upload action deletes orphaned parts that normal expiration rules do not remove.
- Deep Archive for current versions: staff open them daily and restores take hours (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Disabling versioning: it can only be suspended, and the 30-day undo is required (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- One Zone-IA for everything: frequent reads add retrieval fees and minimum storage charges (tốn chi phí hơn)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/intro-lifecycle-rules.html
> 🇻🇳 Bucket bật versioning: hết hạn noncurrent version + abort multipart upload dở dang để giảm chi phí.

A software company runs Amazon Aurora and Amazon DynamoDB databases for 30 applications across 14 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. Finance wants to see database cost per application in AWS Cost Explorer and to receive an email when the forecasted database spend of an application is about to exceed its monthly limit. Engineers already tag every database resource with an application tag. Which TWO actions should a solutions architect take? (Choose TWO)

- A. Activate the application tag separately in the billing console of each of the 14 member accounts.
- B. Activate the application tag as a user-defined cost allocation tag from the management account.
- C. Create a CloudWatch billing alarm on estimated charges in each member account and filter the alarm on the application tag to see forecasted spend.
- D. Create an AWS Budgets cost budget for each application, filtered on the tag, with an alert on forecasted spend.
- E. Deliver an AWS Cost and Usage Report from every member account to its own bucket and email a monthly summary to finance.

- hint: Ba nguồn chi phí khác nhau: phí I/O của Aurora, phí hỗ trợ mở rộng của phiên bản cũ, và nhu cầu cam kết linh hoạt cho tải ổn định.

A SaaS company runs 30 Amazon Aurora MySQL provisioned clusters and 20 Amazon RDS for MySQL 5.7 instances in production. A cost review found that read and write I/O charges are about 40% of the Aurora spend, that the RDS for MySQL 5.7 instances show a monthly Extended Support charge, and that instance usage has been steady for two years. The company will commit for one year with no upfront payment but must stay free to change engines, instance families, and Regions. Which THREE actions will reduce database cost the MOST? (Choose THREE)

- A. Change the Aurora clusters to the Aurora I/O-Optimized configuration so that read and write I/O are no longer billed.
- B. Upgrade the RDS for MySQL 5.7 instances to MySQL 8.0 and stop at that version to end the database Extended Support charge.
- C. Purchase Database Savings Plans with a one-year term and no upfront payment to cover the steady database instance usage.
- D. Purchase three-year All Upfront Reserved Instances for the RDS and Aurora instances that serve read and write traffic, paying the full payment now for steady usage.
- E. Upgrade the RDS for MySQL 5.7 instances through MySQL 8.0 to MySQL 8.4, a major version that is in standard support.
- F. Convert the Aurora clusters to Serverless v2 with a minimum capacity of 0 ACUs so that idle database capacity is not billed.

**Answer:** A, C, E

**Explanation:** I/O-Optimized removes I/O charges when I/O is a large share of Aurora spend, a version in standard support ends Extended Support fees, and Database Savings Plans give a flexible one-year no-upfront discount.
- Stopping at MySQL 8.0: that version is itself in Extended Support now (tốn chi phí hơn)
- Three-year All Upfront Reserved Instances: upfront payment and lock-in to engine and family (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Serverless v2 with 0 ACUs: pausing saves nothing on steady usage (giải bài toán khác)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/extended-support-charges.html
> 🇻🇳 I/O-Optimized khi phí I/O cao; nâng cấp lên phiên bản còn standard support; Database Savings Plans cho tải ổn định, linh hoạt.

- concept: For long retention, keep PITR for the short window and export month-end snapshots to S3 in Parquet with a Glacier lifecycle instead of keeping many snapshots
- refs: 03-database-services.md, F-so-sanh-database-theo-dac-diem.md
- hint: Chỉ cần truy vấn SQL dữ liệu cũ vài lần mỗi năm, không khôi phục vào DB — có cách lưu rẻ hơn snapshot RDS giữ nhiều năm.
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22

A company runs 50 Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL production databases. It keeps point-in-time recovery for 14 days and also keeps a daily manual snapshot of every database for seven years to satisfy an audit rule. Snapshot storage has become the largest part of the database bill. Auditors run SQL queries against old data only a few times a year and accept a one-day delay, and data older than 14 days is never restored into a running database. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

- A. Raise the automated backup retention to the maximum number of days allowed and delete the daily manual snapshots after making that change to each database.
- B. Keep 14 days of automated backups, export month-end snapshots to S3 as Parquet with a Glacier Deep Archive lifecycle rule, and delete the rest.
- C. Keep the daily manual snapshots for seven years and copy each snapshot to a second Region to improve their durability.
- D. Add the databases to an AWS Backup plan whose rule moves the RDS snapshots to cold storage and keeps them for seven years.

**Answer:** B

**Explanation:** Automated backups cover the 14-day recovery need; exported Parquet files in S3 Glacier Deep Archive cost far less than snapshots and can be queried with Athena after a restore, and the other snapshots can be deleted.
- Maximum automated retention: the setting tops out at 35 days, far below seven years (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Daily snapshots plus a second Region: more snapshots and more storage (tốn chi phí hơn)
- AWS Backup cold storage for RDS: not supported for RDS snapshots (cấu hình không tồn tại)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ExportSnapshot.html
> 🇻🇳 PITR cho 14 ngày; lưu 7 năm → export snapshot cuối tháng sang S3 (Parquet) + Glacier Deep Archive, truy vấn bằng Athena.

A genomics lab's sequencers write result files to an SMB share on an on-premises Windows server. The files must appear in Amazon S3 within minutes so that analysts can start Amazon Athena and Amazon EMR jobs, while lab staff keep opening recent files locally with low latency. The sequencer software cannot be changed, and the server has limited disk space. Which solution will meet these requirements?

- A. Schedule an AWS DataSync task at the shortest supported interval to copy new files from the SMB share to the S3 bucket for the analysts
- B. Mount an Amazon EFS file system on the sequencers and use AWS DataSync to copy the result files from EFS to the S3 bucket
- C. Deploy an S3 File Gateway on premises, create an SMB file share backed by the bucket, and point the sequencers at the share
- D. Deploy an AWS Transfer Family SFTP server and have lab staff upload the result files from the Windows server each hour by hand

**Answer:** C

**Explanation:** S3 File Gateway presents an SMB share, uploads each written file to S3 in the background, and keeps recently used data in a local cache, so the sequencers need no change and the server needs little disk.
- DataSync on a schedule: the shortest schedule interval is one hour, longer than minutes (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- EFS mounted on the sequencers: the sequencer software cannot be changed to use it (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Transfer Family with hourly manual uploads: manual work and hourly delay (tốn vận hành hơn)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/task-scheduling.html
> 🇻🇳 File ghi liên tục lên S3 trong vài phút + cache cục bộ → S3 File Gateway; DataSync có lịch tối thiểu 1 giờ.

- domain: cost

- difficulty: hard
- skills: 4.2.k4, 4.2.k9
- concept: A mixed instances policy with an On-Demand base, diversified Spot, price-capacity-optimized allocation and Capacity Rebalancing cuts cost while keeping availability
- refs: 01-compute-services.md, A-nen-tang-kien-truc.md
- hint: Muốn rẻ nhưng không sập khi một pool Spot biến mất — cần nền On-Demand nhỏ, đa dạng loại instance/AZ và chiến lược cấp phát đúng.
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 135

An e-commerce company runs a stateless web tier on an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. All instances are On-Demand instances of a single type across three Availability Zones, and traffic peaks sharply during campaigns. The company wants to reduce compute cost while keeping the site available if Spot capacity in one capacity pool disappears. Which Auto Scaling configuration meets this goal MOST cost-effectively?

- A. Use a mixed instances policy that runs the entire group on Spot Instances across several instance types and three Availability Zones, with no On-Demand base capacity
- B. Keep On-Demand Instances for the whole group and buy Standard Reserved Instances sized for the campaign peak capacity in each Availability Zone
- C. Use a mixed instances policy with a small On-Demand base, Spot above it, several instance types across three zones, price-capacity-optimized allocation and Capacity Rebalancing
- D. Use a mixed instances policy with a small On-Demand base and Spot above it, but keep the current instance type and choose the lowest-price strategy for Spot capacity

**Answer:** C

**Explanation:** The On-Demand base keeps a floor of capacity, diversification spreads Spot across many pools, price-capacity-optimized picks pools that are cheap and unlikely to be interrupted, and Capacity Rebalancing replaces at-risk instances early.
- Spot only with no base: no floor if Spot capacity shrinks (vi phạm ràng buộc).
- Reserved Instances for the peak: paying for peak capacity all year (tốn chi phí hơn).
- One instance type with lowest-price: concentrates capacity in one pool, raising interruption risk (vi phạm ràng buộc).
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/spot-best-practices.html
> 🇻🇳 Spot an toàn: nền On-Demand nhỏ + Spot đa dạng instance/AZ + price-capacity-optimized + Capacity Rebalancing.

- concept: Idle-most-of-the-day bursty stateless work is cheapest on Lambda with on-demand concurrency; provisioned or always-on capacity pays for idle time
- refs: 01-compute-services.md, L-quyet-dinh-nhanh.md
- hint: Rảnh phần lớn thời gian rồi bùng nổ ngắn, request ngắn và chịu được khởi động chậm — trả tiền theo lần chạy hay theo thời gian chờ?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 120

A property-management company runs a service that generates a PDF statement whenever a tenant asks for one. The service is idle for most of the day and then receives bursts of hundreds of requests within a minute. Each request is stateless, finishes in under 10 seconds, uses 1 GB of memory, and tolerates a short startup delay. The service runs on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer, with a minimum of three tasks to absorb bursts. Which solution will reduce compute cost MOST cost-effectively?

- A. Keep the Fargate service behind the load balancer and buy a Compute Savings Plan that covers the three-task baseline
- B. Package the code as a Lambda function and register it as a target of the load balancer with default on-demand concurrency
- C. Move the containers to an EC2 Auto Scaling group behind the load balancer with target tracking and Reserved Instances for the baseline instance
- D. Run the code as a Lambda function behind the load balancer with provisioned concurrency sized for the largest burst

**Answer:** B

**Explanation:** Lambda bills per request and duration, scales out instantly for bursts, and costs nothing while idle, which suits short stateless requests that tolerate a cold start.
- Fargate with a Savings Plan: still pays for three always-on tasks and their commitment (tốn chi phí hơn).
- EC2 Auto Scaling with Reserved Instances: pays for idle baseline instances and adds management (tốn vận hành hơn).
- Provisioned concurrency for the largest burst: pays for idle provisioned capacity (tốn chi phí hơn).
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-limits.html
> 🇻🇳 Tải thưa, bùng nổ ngắn, request ngắn và stateless → Lambda (trả theo lần chạy, về 0 khi rảnh), không dùng provisioned concurrency.

## Q ai-20261022-a42-13
- domain: cost
- task: 4.2
- topic: compute
- services: EC2 Auto Scaling, EC2
- tags: asg-warm-pool, ec2-hibernation, scaling-policies
- difficulty: hard
- skills: 4.2.k9, 4.2.s2
- concept: A Hibernated warm pool keeps RAM contents on EBS so slow-to-initialize instances enter service fast while compute is not billed
- refs: 01-compute-services.md
- hint: Khởi tạo mất 12 phút vì nạp dữ liệu vào RAM — trạng thái pool nào giữ lại RAM mà không tính tiền instance?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 130

A trading analytics company runs an in-memory risk engine on an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group of On-Demand memory-optimized instances. Each instance takes about 12 minutes to load reference data into memory before it can serve requests, so the company keeps extra instances running around the clock to absorb spikes triggered by breaking news. The spikes cannot be predicted. The company wants to cut idle compute cost while still putting new capacity in service within a couple of minutes. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

- A. Add a warm pool with instances in the Stopped state and let the group draw from the pool during scale-out events
- B. Add a warm pool with instances in the Running state and keep them ready for scale-out events at any time
- C. Add a warm pool with instances in the Hibernated state and enable hibernation in the launch template
- D. Add scheduled scaling actions that add capacity shortly before each expected spike in demand

**Answer:** C

**Explanation:** Hibernation writes RAM to the encrypted EBS root volume, so a resumed instance has its data loaded again within minutes, while a hibernated instance incurs charges only for EBS storage and Elastic IPs, not compute.
- Stopped state: instances boot fresh and must reload the 12 minutes of data (vi phạm ràng buộc).
- Running state: pays full compute for idle instances, as before (tốn chi phí hơn).
- Scheduled scaling: the spikes are not predictable (vi phạm ràng buộc).
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-warm-pools.html
> 🇻🇳 Khởi tạo chậm do nạp RAM, spike không đoán trước → warm pool trạng thái Hibernated (giữ RAM trên EBS, không tính tiền compute).
